---
title: "Setup"
subtitle: "Two small Conda environments and one database — about ten minutes, mostly waiting."
---

A little one-time housekeeping: two small Conda environments and one database.
Nextflow and everything else come *inside* the environments, and the toy human
index is already in this repo — so there's no 4 GB download here. Budget ~10
minutes, mostly waiting for Conda.

::: {.callout-warning}
## Read this first — the toy human index is for the tutorial only
To keep things fast, this tutorial dehosts against a *stand-in* human genome — just
the mitochondrion. It is **not** a real dehoster: it will leave almost all human DNA
in your data. **Never use `toy_human` on a real dataset.** For real work, use the
full human genome index (see the [Appendix](appendix.qmd)).
:::

::: {.callout-tip}
## Prerequisites
You need `mamba` (or `conda`) and `git`. If you don't have them, install
[Miniforge](https://github.com/conda-forge/miniforge) — it gives you `mamba`.
Everything below assumes **Linux, macOS, or Windows via WSL**. Wherever you see
`mamba`, plain `conda` works too (just slower).
:::

## 1 · Get the tutorial materials

Clone this repository and move into it — it's your working directory for the whole
tutorial.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hsgweon/resscan-tutorial.git
cd resscan-tutorial
```

Inside, the teaching data is already prepared for you:

| Path | What it is |
| --- | --- |
| `data/rawdata_10K/` | 36 samples × 10,000 read pairs — the reads you'll process |
| `data/host_index/toy_human.*` | Prebuilt toy human index (mitochondrion) — for dehosting |
| `data/reports_full/` | Full-depth results — used in the analysis step |
| `data/read_pairs.csv` | Ready-made VANISH input |

## 2 · Install VANISH

VANISH does the QC and host removal. Clone it and build its environment (this also
installs the `vanish` commands):

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hsgweon/vanish.git tools/vanish
( cd tools/vanish && mamba env create -f environment.yml )
```

## 3 · Install ResScan

ResScan does the AMR quantification. Same pattern:

```bash
git clone https://github.com/hsgweon/resscan.git tools/resscan
( cd tools/resscan && mamba env create -f environment.yml )
```

::: {.callout-note}
## Two tools, two environments
You'll use `vanish-env` for Step 1 and `resscan-env` for Step 2 — **one at a time**.
Always run `mamba deactivate` before switching to the other, so you're never in the
wrong environment.
:::

## 4 · Build the CARD database

ResScan maps reads against [CARD](https://card.mcmaster.ca/). Download it once and
prepare it with ResScan's builder. We pin **v4.0.1** so your results line up with
the full-depth reports used later. Activate `resscan-env` for this, then deactivate
when done:

```bash
mamba activate resscan-env

wget https://card.mcmaster.ca/download/0/broadstreet-v4.0.1.tar.bz2
mkdir -p CARD_raw_v4.0.1
tar -xvjf broadstreet-v4.0.1.tar.bz2 -C CARD_raw_v4.0.1
resscan_build_db -i CARD_raw_v4.0.1 -d resscan_CARD_v4.0.1

mamba deactivate
```

This creates a `resscan_CARD_v4.0.1/` folder — that's the `--card` path you'll pass
to ResScan. It's sub-gigabyte and takes a minute or two to build.

## 5 · Quick check

Confirm each tool is installed. Activate, check, deactivate:

```bash
mamba activate vanish-env
vanish --help | head -3
mamba deactivate

mamba activate resscan-env
resscan --help | head -3
mamba deactivate
```

If both print usage text, you're ready for **Step 1**.
